title: Pin comment claims a broken re-pricing branch would FLIP the route to m2; the math gives count 0 (route vanishes)
detail: Violates the guard: 'the comment says the route "would FLIP to m2" while the documented/actual broken-branch behavior is the route VANISHING (count 0)'. The dist is per-pipe min (branch-independent); a stuck first-seen min_cost=20 fails the equality test for both candidates — count 0.
recommended_fix: Reword the comment: breaking the re-pricing branch leaves min_cost at first-seen 20 while dist stays 5, so both candidates fail the equality test — the route vanishes (count 0), it does not flip to m2.

title: Unguarded hops[off] derefs after the non-fatal count check mis-read a later table row in the pin's own count-0 bite mode
evidence:
core/routing_cost_test.odin:254-258:
	testing.expectf(t, count == 1,
		"the re-priced fat bundle must win UNIQUELY (count 1), got %d", count)
	testing.expectf(t, s.routing.hops[int(off)].node == m1,
		"next hop must be m1 (bundle priced at its min member: 5+5=10), got %d — the bundle edge was NOT re-priced",
		s.routing.hops[int(off)].node)
core/routing_cost_test.odin:286-288:
	testing.expectf(t, s.routing.hops[int(off)].pipe == s.topology.pipe_id[rep_slot],
		"representative Hop.pipe must stay the LOWEST-SLOT member (pipe %d, tier narrow), got %d",
		s.topology.pipe_id[rep_slot], s.routing.hops[int(off)].pipe)
core/routing.odin:245:
			r.hop_offset[idx] = set_start
detail: Guard violation: 'dereferencing `hops[off]` when count == 0 — `testing.expectf` records and CONTINUES'. Under the documented count-0 bite, off = set_start points past the (res,host) entry; hops[off] reads a LATER entry's row, or panics if the entry is last. The run still fails — message quality only.
recommended_fix: Guard the node/pipe asserts with `if ok && count == 1` (Perkins r1 note #3's fix: 'Guard the node asserts with the count condition') so the pinned message is the failure.
